text:
Proper drying after shelling is essential to prevent mould growth (including the risk of aflatoxin contamination -- see the aflatoxin disease topic) and to preserve grain quality in storage. Sun-drying is the most common method: farmers spread shelled kernels in a thin layer (roughly 5 cm deep) over a mat, tarp, or concrete drying floor, and turn/rake the grain regularly (recommended roughly every 1-2 hours during peak sun) to ensure even drying and prevent the surface from baking hard while the inside stays moist.

Where available, mechanical/rental drying facilities offer an alternative to weather-dependent sun-drying, particularly valuable during rainy periods when sun-drying is unreliable; some larger buyers and processors (for example CP Foods, referenced elsewhere in this source in connection with contract corn purchasing) provide or support drying and storage infrastructure that farmers can access through contract-farming or rental arrangements.
